title: Exhaustiveness of alternating column stages
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a bicomplex of $A$-modules with commuting horizontal and vertical differentials of bidegrees $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let $T$ be its coproduct total cochain complex, with total differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$. Suppose every column $p>0$ is zero. For each $j\in\mathbf N$, fix a short complex $S_j=(U_j\xrightarrow{f_j}B_j\xrightarrow{g_j}V_j)$ of cochain complexes and an isomorphism $e_j:B_j\cong K^{-j,\bullet}$. For $n\in\mathbf N$ and $k\in\mathbf Z$, define the submodule $M_n^k$ of $T^k$ as the sum, over $j\in\mathbf N$, of the full image of $K^{-j,k+j}\to T^k$ if $2j+2\le n$, and the image of $U_j^{k+j}\xrightarrow{f_j}B_j^{k+j}\xrightarrow{e_j}K^{-j,k+j}\to T^k$ if $2j+1\le n$; omit a summand when its inequality fails. Then every $x\in T^k$ belongs to $M_n^k$ for some $n\in\mathbf N$. No exactness, splitting, or freeness assumption on the short complexes is needed.

source.place: Tag 09KP, proof, alternating two-step column filtration (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09KP)

proof.text: Each full-column image is contained in stage 2j+2. A positive-column total injection is zero, and every nonpositive column is -j. The total coproduct universal property constructs a linear map to the supremum of stages that is a right inverse of its subtype inclusion. Hence every element belongs to the supremum.
Stage monotonicity makes the submodule family directed. Apply Mathlib Submodule.mem_iSup_of_directed to convert supremum membership into membership in a single stage.
